newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemala fires more police in corruption scandal.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala fires more police in corruption scandal.

text.p: The Guatemalan government on Tuesday fired 12 police officers, including five regional police chiefs implicated in an ever-widening corruption scandal that broke last week, the interior minister said.

"Today, as a consequence of advances in the investigation that is being realised, we took the decision to fire 12 more officers of the National Police," Interior Minister Rodolfo Mendoza told reporters.
The dismissals come one week after an unprecedented purge of 19 police, customs and army officials, including two generals, one of them the deputy defence minister.
The dismissals stem from an investigation into an enormous smuggling operation of alleged crime boss Alfredo Moreno, a former army intelligence officer who was arrested on Sept. 15.

Interior Minister Mendoza said an investigation by the Attorney General's Office found evidence that the police officials fired on Tuesday had maintained constant communication with Moreno. He said prosecutors must seek arrest warrants and bring charges against the fired officers.
The officers fired on Tuesday include police chiefs of Peten, Chimaltenango, Salama, Izabal and San Marcos provinces as well as the deputy chief of the police personnel department.
Finance Minister Jose Alejandro Arevalo said the contraband ring cheated the government of an estimated $15 million a month, roughly equivalent to the yearly public health budget.
According to newspapers, a constant stream of trucks loaded with merchandise entered the country without paying duties.
Moreno is the only person arrested and facing charges in the case. He spent five days in a hospital after his capture but was moved to a Guatemalay City prison over the weekend.
The right-wing opposition party Guatemalan Republican Front has admitted that Moreno contributed more than $10,000 to the party's 1995 presidential campaign.
